title: fix(pm): an UNJUDGED `--pair` names the channel that answered, what it answered, and which carrier
body:
Fixes #16833

Clause-②: no

Scope: the **revised rank 1** of triage comment `5610592774` and nothing else — «Make the gate report which channel answered, and why it could not read». ⛔ Rank 2 (diagnosing why one container 403s while others 200) and rank 3 (reading the clear's provenance comment) are **not** addressed here and are not touched.

## What moved

`check-clause2-carriers --pair` answers exit 2 / UNJUDGED when a carrier's label event stream cannot be read. That answer is correct and stays. What the message could not say was **why**: a `403` in one container, a `404`, a rate limit, a transport fault with no status at all, and a `--pair-json` document that simply omits the `events` key all rendered as the same sentence. Two of the three containers that re-took the card's own reading answered `200`, so "the stream is unreachable" was a **global assumption** standing in for a **per-seat fact**.

Every read this run could not complete is now recorded **where it fails** — the channel it was tried on, in the path report's own `(i)` / `(ii)` / `(iii)` spelling, and what the platform answered on it — and rides on the pair as `pair.reads`. The three UNJUDGED sentences this file prints (`pairUnjudged`, `wideningUnjudged`, `locatedRecordUnjudged`) append it, so a refusal names the **channel**, the **answer** and the **carrier** together.

Measured, this container, `/events` answering 403 while every other read answers 200:

```
✗ check-clause2-carriers --pair: pair PR #13910 / card #13476 — UNJUDGED: card #13476's label
event stream, PR #13910's label event stream could not be read. An unread carrier is not a bare
carrier and an unread thread is not an absent declaration; this pair is missing from the readings
above, not clean in them. Channel diagnosis, one entry per read this run could not complete:
card #13476's label event stream — (i) token answered HTTP 403, then (ii) token-less public read
answered HTTP 403 (2× — the same answer on every attempt); PR #13910's label event stream —
(ii) token-less public read answered HTTP 403 (2× — the same answer on every attempt). ⛔ A channel
that refused is a measured fact about THIS seat's access to THAT resource and about nothing else …
```

## The two non-negotiable constraints, and how this PR holds them

1. **The UNJUDGED answer stays available.** No predicate reads `pair.reads`; no evidence source is added. The diagnosis is appended to the verdict, never instead of it. Pinned in both directions (below), including a control that a *readable* pair's output is byte-identical to the pre-change script's.
2. **⛔ Not verdict-reading.** Nothing here reads a comment, a verdict value, or a `Served-tier:` line it did not already read. The only new inputs are HTTP statuses, transport error text and the document's own missing keys.

## Exit codes — unchanged, measured in both directions

Same three fixtures run against `origin/main`'s copy of the script (`e46ac0fb6`) and against this branch:

| fixture | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `--pair 13910 --pair-json` with the `events` bag **omitted** (unread stream) | exit **2**, UNJUDGED | exit **2**, UNJUDGED |
| the same document with `events` **present** (readable) | exit **4** (C3 row) | exit **4** (C3 row), output **byte-identical** |
| live path, platform answering `403` on `/events` alone, `200` elsewhere | exit **2**, UNJUDGED | exit **2**, UNJUDGED |

The only textual delta on the two unread runs is the appended diagnosis; `diff` of the readable run is empty.

## Self-test battery floor — probed, never estimated

The floor was read by parsing the roster out of both revisions, with a firing control taken the same way on the same file (a battery this diff does not move):

| reading | `origin/main` `e46ac0fb6` | this branch |
|:--|:--|:--|
| declared batteries | 26 | **27** |
| `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` | 25 | **26** |
| sum of per-battery case floors | 654 | **684** |
| ⛔ CONTROL — `the exit register is distinct in every direction it must be` | 6 | 6 (unmoved) |

Cases run: **715 → 745**, exit 0 both. The new battery is pinned at 30.

## Ablation ledger — each new behaviour mutated until it lies, then restored

Each leg: mutate → prove it landed on disk by anchor counts → run the battery → restore with `git checkout HEAD --` → prove the restore with `git hash-object` against the HEAD blob **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`. A `trap` on `EXIT INT TERM` restores on any interruption; an empty hash is treated as FAILURE, not as success.

| leg | mutation | anchor on disk | battery | restore |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | the channel is always reported as `(i) token` | anchor 1 → 0, injected → 1 | **RED**, 4 of 745 | `ed7d952d…` == HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty |
| A2 | the platform's answer is dropped from the render | anchor 1 → 0, injected → 1 | **RED**, 10 of 745 | same hash, empty diff |
| A3 | the carrier's name is replaced by a constant | anchor 1 → 0, injected → 1 | **RED**, 3 of 745 | same hash, empty diff |

⚠️ A3 is the reason the second commit exists. On its first run it reddened **one** case, because the gap list above the diagnosis already names the carrier — so the case that merely grepped for the carrier stayed green on a message with no diagnosis at all. Both such cases now pin the carrier **adjacent to the channel that refused it**, and A3 reddens 3.

## Changeset — measured, with a firing control

`skip-changeset`. The criterion is whether anything **published** moves. Every non-private manifest's `files[]` was walked (70 of them) and the touched path placed against each shipped entry:

```
scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs => NOT SHIPPED by any non-private files[]
packages/lint/CHANGELOG.md            => @objectstack/lint (CHANGELOG.md)   ← firing control
```

The control fires on the exact reflex this repo warns about (`packages/lint` ships its `CHANGELOG.md`), so the zero above is a reading rather than a dead probe.

## Clause-② — re-judged from the diff, not from the card

`Clause-②: no`. The diff adds three module-level exports to an internal PM script (`renderReadDiagnosis`, `readDiagnosisKey`, `READ_PATH_LABELS`) and touches no `packages/spec`, no published `exports`, no closed set and no registry entry. The machine reading is **NOT MEASURED**, honestly reported: `check-widening-tells --declaration no` on this diff answers `1 changed file(s) — 0 judged against a declared surface, 1 NOT MEASURED — no declared surface covers scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs`. ⛔ That exit 0 is evidence about no surface at all, and is not read here as a clean one.

⚠️ The tier notice on the card (`5612083405`) refers to "its `Clause-②: yes` declaration". That string's source is triage comment `5582795282`, where it **quotes the gate's own C3 candidate shape** («declared `Clause-②: yes`, gate on neither carrier») — it is not a declaration by the card. This PR declares from its diff.

## Gates

All families derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `8c56e21e8` (36 commands) were run and reconciled with `--ran`. 35 exit 0; `check:pm-dispatch-gates` (the ~1700-case battery) was detached and waited on by recorded PID — its verdict is in the report on the card.

## Acceptance notes

- `noted, not filed: the `--pair-json` refusal names the document by the path the caller typed, so an absolute scratch path can make the sentence long. It is the correct name (a document named twice under different paths is two documents), and shortening it would cost the reproducibility the path buys. Carrier: none — no open PR and no queued card touches this file's reader.`
